messages:
anya: Pushed a quick prototype for the onboarding flow — question: telemetry + sample-projects consent. Do we want a blocking modal during setup, or a subtle banner/toggle inside the checklist?

morgan: my vote: banner inside checklist. Keeps momentum. modal feels interruptive when people just want to try sample projects.

lee: +1 for non-blocking, but we need explicit opt-in wording. If it's a banner, make the primary action opt-in, not hidden. Also add a link to details (privacy page).

scott: legal flagged that any analytics that could even theoretically be tied to a user needs explicit consent in EU. Wording matters. @legal-bot any quick guidance?

legal-bot: short: prefer explicit affirmative action. Banner is OK if the CTA is explicit ("Yes, share anonymized usage"). Avoid pre-checked boxes. Include a link to the privacy page and store consent server-side tied to account.

dev-bot: technical: if we do banner, it can fire `telemetry.consent_shown` + `telemetry.consent_response` events. Implementation note: store preference as account setting so it surfaces in Settings -> Privacy. If they opt in, we attach `x-telemetry-opted-in: true` to example request headers for sample projects.

anya: copying two small variants so we can A/B later:

Variant A (banner inline in checklist):

[Banner]
Help us improve Redwood Inference with anonymous usage data.
[Primary CTA] Yes, share anonymized usage (recommended)
[Secondary] No thanks · Learn more

Variant B (modal, shown after checklist completes):

Modal header: Help improve Redwood
Body: We collect anonymous usage to improve performance and product prioritization. No request bodies are stored. Opt in?
[Primary CTA] Opt in
[Secondary] Skip — opt out

lee: copy nit: "No request bodies are stored" sounds defensive. Suggest: "We only collect anonymized usage metrics; request content is never stored." clearer and stronger.

morgan: UX nit on Variant A: primary CTA text could bias. Maybe neutral label "Share anonymized usage" so it's explicit but not too persuasive. Also make the recommended label smaller (i.e., subtext) instead of in the button.

anya: good call. also accessibility: if we use modal, ensure we don't trap keyboard focus forever and allow Esc to close. If banner, ensure the banner is reachable via skip-nav and has aria-live for confirmation message after clicking.

scott: for sample projects we need a separate opt-in toggle. Some teams will want sample projects but not telemetry. Proposal:
- During onboarding show a single row in checklist: "Sample projects & telemetry"
- Inline two toggles: [Include sample projects] [Share anonymized usage]
This keeps choices granular.

lee: UI nit: two toggles in one row will look cluttered on mobile. Maybe stack them or collapse under a "More settings" expander.

anya: mock attached (link): https://figma.redwood/proto/onboard-telemetry (pretend link). Quick keyboard flow:
1) Tab to banner -> focus on primary -> press Enter -> show toast "Thanks — you can change this in Settings > Privacy" (announce with aria-live)
2) If they press "Learn more" open privacy page in new tab; keep onboarding flow active.

morgan: change event names we agreed on: `telemetry.consent_shown`, `telemetry.consent_given`, `telemetry.consent_revoked`, `sample_projects.provisioned` — dev-bot pls confirm payload shape

dev-bot: payloads proposed:
```
{ "event": "telemetry.consent_given", "user_id": "<id>", "method": "onboarding_banner", "timestamp": 168... }
```
Keep personally-identifying fields out. Send `region` and `product_version` only.

legal-bot: confirm storage: keep consent record (user_id, consent_boolean, timestamp, method) for audit. If EU user opts out, ensure we don't send sample request headers.

anya: accessibility checklist for final build:
- buttons have accessible names
- banner is reachable via `role=\"region\"` with `aria-label=\"Telemetry settings\"`
- toasts announced via `aria-live=\"polite\"`
- keyboard: Esc closes modal; Tab order logical; focus returns to checklist control after close
- color contrast for banner CTA meets WCAG AA

scott: one more UX: when someone chooses "Include sample projects", we should surface a small callout: "These example projects may send anonymized example requests to our servers to populate logs. You can disable telemetry anytime." helps transparency.

morgan: thoughts on default states? legal wants explicit opt-in, so default for telemetry should be OFF. sample projects default ON? That might surprise users. I'd default sample projects ON but explain what they do in the row.

lee: prefer default sample projects OFF too — less surprising. We have free credits and demos; people expect sample projects to work. But ok if privacy baseline is conservative: both OFF by default, with clear CTA to enable.

anya: ok decision proposal (TL;DR):
- Use inline banner inside checklist (non-blocking) with granular controls available via a small row or an expander.
- Telemetry default OFF; sample projects default OFF.
- Primary button text: "Share anonymized usage" (explicit), secondary: "No thanks" plus "Learn more" link.
- Store consent server-side and expose toggle in Settings -> Privacy.
- Accessibility checklist enforced before merge.

morgan: agree. can we get a short copy iteration for the banner that legal-lint approves? I'll file a follow PR with two short options.

legal-bot: I'll review short copy in PR. Also flagging for privacy team FYI.

anya: thanks all — I'll update the prototype and post the next mock. leaving a small TODO: compact mobile layout for two-row expander, and microcopy for the sample-projects callout. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: noted: creating ticket INF-4226 with event names and API contract.

scott: merging consensus. ship it behind a feature flag for 2 weeks and collect metrics on conversion and support tickets.

anya: added feature-flag note to the PR. End thread.
